convention: e^{jωt}; ε_r = ε′ − jε″; φ = 0 is the bearing from the stem's axis through the node

outputs.field_same_current_dB: |F(φ)|² — the far field with the tree against the same source current without it; EXACT in the horizontal plane for a short dipole (TM) or small loop (TE) along an infinite stem (k_z = 0)
outputs.gain_dB: |F(φ)|²/(P_in/P₀) — the same field at equal INPUT power; 2-D normalisation, an indicator
outputs.efficiency: P_rad/P_in in 2-D — an indicator of the near-field loss, not the 3-D antenna efficiency

polarization.TM: an electric line current along the stem — E along the stem
polarization.TE: a magnetic line current along the stem — E horizontal

verdict: In the horizontal plane, with the gateway straight behind the stem the field of a short dipole along the stem (TM) is 10.7–34.5 dB below its level with the gateway in front, and its deepest null lies 13.4–54.4 dB below the front at 138.15–180.0° from it; at 90° it is 6.1–9.4 dB down, and it stays within 3 dB of the front only to 54–66°. A dipole tangential to the bark (TE, horizontal E): 7.7–48.0 dB behind, 9.2–21.1 dB at 90°. Ranges span every reading of the stem's permittivity, diameter and the antenna's standoff in this cache. The 2-D efficiency indicator — what the near field loses into the stem — is 0.14–0.70 (TM) and 0.15–0.54 (TE); it is not the 3-D antenna efficiency.
